name: Rava Dosa
cuisine: South Indian (Karnataka/Tamil Nadu Udupi-hotel classic; a staple of Mumbai's Udupi restaurants)

ingredients.name: Semolina (rava / sooji), fine or medium (Bombay rava)
Water
ingredients.householdMeasure: about ¾ cup + 2 tbsp (added in parts)

ingredients.name: Onion, finely chopped
ingredients.householdMeasure: ½ small onion (about ⅓ cup chopped)

ingredients.name: Sunflower oil (or ghee; groundnut oil is also common)

equipment: Flat tawa (dosa pan), at least 25 cm wide
Mixing bowl (medium, with room to whisk)
Ladle or small steel cup (katori, about 100 ml) for pouring; no ladle: pour from a small steel glass
Measuring spoons and a measuring cup; no set: a normal tablespoon/teaspoon and a 200 ml steel glass (about 1 glass of water)
Half an onion or a paper towel to grease the tawa (cut onion dipped in oil works on cast iron)
Small bowl of water and a wet cloth (cast iron only, to cool and wipe the tawa between dosas)

steps.title: Measure the flours
steps.text: Put 25 g (2½ tbsp) rava, 25 g (3 tbsp) rice flour and 10 g (1 heaped tbsp) maida in the mixing bowl.
steps.visualCue: Three small heaps in the bowl: cream rava, white rice flour, white maida
steps.cameraCheck: The bowl with the three flours
steps.videoShot: Spoons of each flour going into the bowl.
steps.watchOut: Mixing up rice flour and maida by eye (both white); use separate spoons, because too much maida makes a soft, chewy dosa instead of a crisp one

steps.title: Add the dry spices
steps.text: Add ¼ tsp salt, ¼ tsp cumin seeds and ¼ tsp coarsely crushed black pepper.
steps.visualCue: Brown cumin and black pepper bits sitting on top of the flour
steps.cameraCheck: The bowl from above
steps.videoShot: Crushed pepper sprinkled over the flour.
steps.watchOut: Finely powdered pepper disappears into the batter and tastes harsh; crush it coarsely so you can see bits

steps.title: Mix the dry ingredients
steps.text: Stir with a spoon so the flours and spices blend.
steps.visualCue: One even pale mixture with spice specks spread through it
steps.cameraCheck: The mixed flour
steps.videoShot: Spoon turning the flour.
steps.watchOut: Streaks of pure rice flour left unmixed, which show up later as lumps; keep stirring until no white streaks remain

steps.title: Add the curd and the first water
steps.text: Add 1 tbsp (15 g) curd and 120 ml (½ cup) water.
steps.visualCue: A thick, lumpy paste
steps.cameraCheck: The bowl with curd and water added
steps.videoShot: Water poured in over the curd.
steps.watchOut: Pouring all the water at once, which makes lumps harder to remove; add only this first 120 ml now

steps.title: Whisk until smooth
steps.text: Whisk well, pressing out lumps against the side of the bowl.
steps.tip: Remove lumps now while the batter is thick; it is much harder once it is watery.
steps.visualCue: No dry lumps; a smooth, thick batter like pancake batter
steps.cameraCheck: The batter dripping off the whisk
steps.videoShot: The whisk lifting smooth batter.
steps.watchOut: Small dry pockets hiding at the bottom of the bowl; scrape the base with the whisk, and if any remain, press them with the back of a spoon

steps.title: Thin the batter
steps.text: Add another 70 ml (about 5 tbsp) water and whisk again.
steps.visualCue: Very thin and watery, like buttermilk (chaas); it runs off the spoon in a thin stream, not blobs
steps.cameraCheck: The batter poured from a spoon
steps.videoShot: Batter running off the ladle in a thin stream.
steps.watchOut: A batter that is still thick (it coats the spoon like cream), which gives a soft, holeless dosa; add 1 tbsp water at a time until it flows thinly

steps.title: Chop the onion
steps.text: Finely chop 40 g (½ small) onion and keep it in a small bowl.
steps.visualCue: Small even pieces about the size of a rice grain
steps.cameraCheck: ⅓ cup chopped onion in a bowl
steps.videoShot: Knife chopping onion finely.
steps.watchOut: Big onion chunks, which make the dosa tear and stay raw; chop fine

steps.title: Chop the aromatics
steps.text: Finely chop 1 small green chilli, ½ inch ginger, 6-8 curry leaves and 1 tbsp coriander.
steps.visualCue: Four small green-and-yellow heaps on the board
steps.cameraCheck: The chopped chilli, ginger, curry leaves and coriander
steps.videoShot: Knife running through curry leaves.
steps.watchOut: Large ginger or chilli pieces that burn or bite hard in a thin dosa; chop them as fine as the onion

steps.title: Add the aromatics to the batter
steps.text: Stir the chilli, ginger, curry leaves and coriander into the batter (keep the onion for the tawa).
steps.visualCue: Green flecks spread through the thin batter
steps.cameraCheck: The batter with greens
steps.videoShot: Herbs stirred into the batter.
steps.watchOut: Adding the onion here; it releases water and makes the dosa soft, so keep it separate

steps.title: Rest the batter
steps.text: Leave the bowl uncovered on the counter.
steps.tip: The rava soaks up water while resting, so the batter thickens a little. No fermentation is needed.
steps.visualCue: The rava has settled at the bottom and the top looks watery
steps.cameraCheck: The resting batter
steps.videoShot: The bowl sitting next to a timer.
steps.watchOut: Skipping the rest; the rava stays gritty and the dosa tastes sandy and breaks. If you are in a hurry, rest at least 15 minutes

steps.title: Check and adjust the batter
steps.text: Stir from the bottom. If it has thickened, add 1-2 tbsp water (up to about 210 ml in total).
steps.visualCue: Back to a thin, buttermilk-like flow with the rava lifted from the bottom
steps.cameraCheck: Batter flowing off the ladle
steps.videoShot: Ladle lifting and dropping thin batter.
steps.watchOut: Skipping this check; a thickened batter gives a dense dosa. If it already pours thinly, add nothing

steps.title: Heat the tawa
steps.text: Put the tawa on medium-high heat.
steps.visualCue: A few drops of water sizzle and vanish within 2-3 seconds
steps.cameraCheck: Water drops sizzling on the tawa
steps.videoShot: Water flicked onto the hot tawa, hissing.
steps.watchOut: A tawa that is too cool (water just sits and slowly steams) makes the batter stick and tear; wait longer. A smoking tawa is too hot; lower the heat for 30 seconds

steps.title: Season the tawa
steps.text: Rub a few drops of oil over the tawa with a cut onion half or paper towel. (Cast iron: then sprinkle a little water and wipe it off with a wet cloth.)
steps.tip: On non-stick, a few drops wiped with a paper towel is enough.
steps.visualCue: A thin even sheen, no pools of oil
steps.cameraCheck: The shiny tawa
steps.videoShot: Onion half rubbing oil across the tawa.
steps.watchOut: Too much oil, which pools and fries the batter unevenly; wipe off the extra

steps.title: Sprinkle the onion
steps.text: Scatter half the chopped onion (20 g) over the centre of the tawa in a rough circle.
steps.visualCue: Onion bits spread over an area about 20 cm wide
steps.cameraCheck: Onion on the tawa
steps.videoShot: Hand scattering onion over the tawa.
steps.watchOut: Piling the onion in one clump, which leaves a thick patch that will not crisp; spread it thinly

steps.title: Stir the batter
steps.text: Stir the batter well from the bottom right before pouring.
steps.visualCue: The settled rava is lifted back into the batter and the batter looks evenly cloudy
steps.cameraCheck: The ladle scraping the bottom of the bowl
steps.videoShot: Ladle stirring from the bottom.
steps.watchOut: Not stirring; the first dosa comes out watery and the last one all rava. Stir before every pour

steps.title: Pour the dosa
steps.text: Take about half the batter (one ladle, about 120 ml). From about 15 cm above the tawa, pour it in a thin stream, starting at the outer edge and moving in circles towards the centre. Fill only big gaps; small holes are wanted. Do not spread it with the ladle.
steps.tip: Pouring from the outside in gives a crisp even edge.
steps.visualCue: A lacy net-like circle with many small holes that sizzles immediately
steps.cameraCheck: The freshly poured dosa
steps.videoShot: Batter streaming from a height into a lacy circle.
steps.watchOut: Batter that does not sizzle (tawa too cool), or a solid sheet with no holes (batter too thick or ladle used to spread). Rescue: thin the batter with 1-2 tbsp water for the next dosa

steps.title: Add the oil
steps.text: Drizzle 1 tsp (5 ml) oil around the edge and over the holes.
steps.visualCue: Oil bubbling in the holes and at the edges
steps.cameraCheck: The oil drizzle on the dosa
steps.videoShot: Oil dropped from a spoon around the dosa.
steps.watchOut: Skipping the oil, which leaves a pale, papery dosa that sticks; add it right after pouring

steps.title: Cook until crisp
steps.text: Cook on medium-high without touching it.
steps.tip: Flipping is optional; hotels usually do not flip.
steps.visualCue: The top looks dry and set, the base is golden-brown, and the edges lift from the tawa on their own
steps.cameraCheck: The lifted golden edge
steps.videoShot: Edge curling up from the tawa.
steps.watchOut: Lifting too early, which tears the dosa; wait for the edges to curl. If the underside is pale after 4 minutes the tawa is too cool; raise the heat a little

steps.title: Fold and remove
steps.text: Slide the spatula under the dosa, fold it in half (or roll it), and lift it onto a plate.
steps.visualCue: A crisp golden lacy dosa that holds its shape
steps.cameraCheck: The folded dosa on the plate
steps.videoShot: Spatula folding and lifting the dosa.
steps.watchOut: A soft, pale centre that bends limply; put it back for 30 seconds and it usually crisps

steps.title: Reset the tawa
steps.text: Reduce the heat for 20 seconds (cast iron: sprinkle water and wipe), then turn it back to medium-high.
steps.visualCue: A clean tawa with no burnt bits; water sizzles again before you pour
steps.cameraCheck: The clean tawa
steps.videoShot: Wet cloth wiping the tawa.
steps.watchOut: Pouring the next dosa on a still-cooling or crumb-covered tawa, which makes it stick; wait until a water drop sizzles

steps.title: Make the second dosa
steps.text: Repeat steps 14 to 19 with the remaining onion, batter (stir first) and 1 tsp oil.
steps.visualCue: Same golden lacy dosa
steps.cameraCheck: Two dosas on the plate
steps.videoShot: The second lacy dosa crisping.
steps.watchOut: Rushing the second dosa because the first was good; the tawa may have run too hot, so recheck the water-drop sizzle

steps.title: Serve at once
steps.text: Serve hot with coconut chutney and/or sambar.
steps.visualCue: Crisp dosas that crackle when torn
steps.cameraCheck: The plate with dosas and sides
steps.videoShot: Hand tearing a crackling piece of dosa.
steps.watchOut: Letting it sit; rava dosa goes soft within 5-10 minutes. Serve straight from the tawa

researchRating.basis: rava dosa is one of the most-ordered Udupi dishes, appears in Mumbai "best dosa" guides, and every major Indian recipe site and many blogs carry an instant, no-fermentation version (still the case in this cycle's searches, including a Feb 2026 blog post). Points are lost for the common complaints of sticking, tearing or turning soft when the batter is too thick or the tawa too cool. Star counts on individual recipe sites could not be re-read this cycle (sites blocked), so the rating is held at the previous 4.3 on the strength of the unchanged sentiment.

storage: Cooked dosas are best not stored; they turn soft and leathery. If you must, refrigerate in a closed box up to 1 day and reheat on a hot tawa 1 minute per side. Not suitable for the freezer. Leftover batter: fridge, covered, up to 1 day (add onion only on the tawa). Stir well and add 2-4 tbsp water before using, because the rava keeps absorbing water.
leftoverRemix: Rava dosa kothu. Tear 1-2 leftover dosas into small pieces. Fry ½ chopped onion, ½ chopped tomato and a pinch of chilli powder and garam masala in 1 tsp oil, add the dosa pieces and 2 tbsp leftover sambar, and toss on high heat for 2 minutes until coated and lightly crisp. Top with coriander and lemon.
burnOff: about 4.7 km of running (330 ÷ 70 kcal/km, 70 kg adult), or about 6.6 km of brisk walking (about 80 minutes at 5 km/h, at about 50 kcal/km) (est.). With sambar and chutney (about 500 kcal): about 7.1 km running or 10 km walking (est.).

navratri.reason: semolina (wheat), rice flour and maida are grains, not eaten on the common vrat rule set (onion is also avoided); a vrat dosa would be a different dish (samak rice or kuttu flour)

ekadashi.reason: contains rice flour and wheat, and grains, especially rice, are avoided on Ekadashi (common rule set assumed)

jain.reason: skip onion and fresh ginger and use sonth or nothing; Mumbai menus sell "Jain Rava Dosa" (seen in the previous version on Zomato and magicpin; not re-confirmed this cycle)

ramadan.reason: vegetarian (no halal concern) and light; it is mostly refined carbohydrate, so pair it with dal-based sambar for sehri to stay full longer

jain.reason: skip the onion and fresh ginger (root vegetables) and use a pinch of dry ginger powder (sonth) or none; no garlic, potato or hing is used
